teaching.hint: If two adjacent values rise, what must eventually happen farther in that direction?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: An adjacent slope certifies a peak on one side when the retained interval has outward-decreasing boundary slopes; sortedness is unnecessary.
solution_outline.approach: Keep an interval. Compare its midpoint with the next value: retain the right half after an increase, or the left half including the midpoint after a decrease. Stop when one index remains.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The left endpoint is greater than its outside left neighbor, and the right endpoint is greater than its outside right neighbor, using negative infinity at array boundaries.
solution_outline.correctness: The boundary conditions force a peak inside: an increasing walk must eventually descend before passing the right boundary, or a decreasing walk must reverse before passing the left boundary. A rising midpoint pair creates the needed new left boundary; a falling pair creates the new right boundary. Hence every retained interval preserves both conditions, and at a singleton they certify that exact index as a whole-array peak.
solution_outline.complexity: O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: The search uses comparisons, not value differences, which may overflow; adjacent distinctness is essential to the direction certificate.

common_wrong_turns: The search uses comparisons, not value differences, which may overflow; adjacent distinctness is essential to the direction certificate.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained the explicit logarithmic requirement, any-answer semantics, adjacent distinctness, and outside-neighbor convention; made boundary certificates explicit in the outline.
